stories.title: One dose of a psychedelic nasal spray eased hard to treat depression in a trial
stories.summary: A JAMA trial at 38 sites gave 193 adults whose depression had not improved after two to five antidepressants a single nasal spray of mebufotenin, or 5-MeO-DMT, which reduced symptoms, Yahoo Health reports. Its effects peak within 15 minutes and usually fade within an hour.

stories.title: Researchers propose circadian depression as a possible subtype
stories.summary: A study in the British Journal of Psychiatry by Australian researchers suggests that for some people, staying up late, sleeping long and waking exhausted may mark a distinct form of depression driven by a disrupted body clock, National Geographic reports. The subtype is still a proposal.

stories.title: A weakened brain signal may link several schizophrenia symptoms
stories.summary: McGill University scientists identified a weakened brain signal that may connect seemingly unrelated symptoms of schizophrenia, including sensory processing difficulties and disorganised speech, ScienceDaily reports. They say it could help explain the condition and potentially lead to earlier detection.

stories.title: Aparna Piramal Raje on living a full life with bipolar disorder
stories.summary: Writer and bestselling author Aparna Piramal Raje has lived with bipolar disorder for over two decades. In a piece published in partnership with the India Mental Health Alliance, she shares what helps her, from her family's love to a sleep routine she treats as sacred.

stories.title: Northern Ireland police will hand more mental health calls to health staff
stories.summary: The PSNI handles about 30,000 mental health calls a year. From November it will stop welfare checks unless there is a risk to life, harm or a crime, and handlers may pass calls to health and social care staff, the BBC reports. Reaction has been mixed.

stories.title: A psychologist argues emotion dysregulation sits at the root of ADHD
stories.summary: Writing in Psychology Today, a clinician argues that research points to emotion dysregulation as a root of ADHD, which may explain the attention symptoms and why ADHD often appears with other conditions. Focusing on it, the piece says, could guide more effective treatment.

stories.title: One clown visit nearly halved sadness scores in adult hospital patients
stories.summary: In Colombia, 40 adults on an internal medicine ward each got one 20 minute visit from the same pair of healthcare clowns. Their average sadness score fell by almost half, and anxiety and anger dropped too. Forty patients is a small study, and scores were taken right afterwards.

stories.title: What the evidence says about creatine and mental health
stories.summary: Creatine's benefits for strength are well supported, and it is increasingly being recommended for mental health, with a recent review suggesting possible benefits as a depression treatment, a piece republished by inkl reports. The evidence for mood is newer than the evidence for muscle.

stories.title: Meta settles a teen's social media mental health claim before trial
stories.summary: Meta settled with a teen plaintiff who said Instagram and Facebook were designed to be addictive and harmed her mental health, her attorneys said on Friday. Meta had settled with a second teen days earlier, so the trial is expected to proceed against Snap only.

stories.title: Jagruti Rehabilitation Centre raises Rs 28 crore
stories.summary: Jagruti, which describes itself as one of India's largest organised mental health, addiction and dementia care platforms, has raised Rs 28 crore in its first institutional round, led by Alkemi Growth Capital, BW Disrupt reports.

stories.title: Punjab makes registration mandatory for mental health establishments
stories.summary: Punjab's health department has told mental health establishments to register with the State Mental Health Authority under the Mental Healthcare Act, 2017, warning that failure to comply may invite action, the Times of India reports. The aim is effective implementation of the Act.

stories.title: Mandi college students take mental health awareness to the street
stories.summary: The psychology department of Vallabh Government College, Mandi, staged a street play called Mental Health of the Common Man to encourage people to seek help without hesitation, based on the WHO theme for World Mental Health Day 2026, The Tribune reports.

stories.title: Personalised music with beats lowered cortisol more than pink noise
stories.summary: A randomised trial at Toronto Metropolitan University found 24 minutes of personalised music paired with auditory beat stimulation lowered the stress hormone cortisol more than twice as much as pink noise, a popular relaxation sound, Medical Xpress reports.

stories.title: Meditation and VR training led to more lucid dreams in a small study
stories.summary: University of Trento researchers trained students with meditation, reality checks and virtual reality scenes where objects broke the laws of physics. Doing this twice a week for a month led to lucid dreams four times as often as reality checks alone, Live Science reports.

stories.title: People remember a hug for how it made them feel
stories.summary: A PLOS One study of 15,049 UK adults led by the University of Bristol found people were more likely to remember a hug because it made them feel comforted, supported or understood than because of the gesture itself, the Times of India reports.

stories.title: Twenty minutes of music may ease pain and low mood, a review finds
stories.summary: A BMC Psychology meta-analysis of nine randomised trials in 787 patients with pain found 20 minutes of music can help relieve pain and associated depression symptoms, the Express reports. It worked best when patients chose their own music.

stories.title: Sky and trees help campus stress recovery, up to a point
stories.summary: Researchers in Nanning, China, paired over a thousand campus walkway photos with students' ratings and found the restorative effect of greenery did not keep rising with more green in view, and open sky had limits too, in Computational Urban Science.

stories.title: Mindful.org on working with fear instead of fighting it
stories.summary: A Mindful.org piece looks at everyday fears, from walking alone at night to a lingering headache, and how mindful attention can change our relationship with them. Fear, it notes, on bad days cripples us and on good days is simply annoying.

stories.title: How to recover from a very public mistake
stories.summary: In the Guardian, Gaby Hinsliff writes about NHS surgeon and author Gabriel Weston, who shared candidly how a serious mistake at work left her feeling ashamed and alone, and argues that recovery from public failure comes through remorse rather than shamelessness.

stories.title: Greater Good's happiness calendar for November
stories.summary: The Greater Good Science Center at Berkeley has published its monthly Happiness Calendar, a day by day guide to wellbeing. November's edition is meant to help readers pause and notice good things.

stories.title: Healthy sleep duration linked to a younger biological age
stories.summary: A Nature study using data from about half a million adults in the MULTI Consortium examined sleep duration and biological age gaps, the difference between how old the body seems and how old it is, SSBCrack reports. The study shows associations.

stories.title: For menopausal insomnia, CBT-I held up against pills in a review
stories.summary: A systematic review found non drug approaches were robust first line options for chronic insomnia in peri and postmenopausal women, Psychiatric Times reports. Indirect comparisons suggested CBT-I works about as well as Z drugs, contrary to what the investigators expected.

stories.title: One in four online reviewers stopped a newer insomnia drug
stories.summary: Rutgers researchers analysed hundreds of online reviews of the prescription insomnia drug lemborexant and found about one in four reviewers stopped or planned to stop taking it, News-Medical reports. Insomnia affects about 30 per cent of adults.

stories.title: How sleep changes as we age
stories.summary: As the body clock shifts with age, sleep often becomes lighter and more interrupted, according to the US National Institute on Aging, a Stacker piece from BetterSleep explains. That does not mean the need for rest disappears.

stories.title: Five hours of sleep for three nights, filmed
stories.summary: In Bupa's Health or Hype video series, fitness advocate Joe Wicks cut his sleep to about five hours a night for three nights while sleep specialist Dr Sophie Bostock watched. His screen time passed 13.5 hours a day and carbohydrate cravings rose.

stories.title: Diet and sleep should be studied together, an editorial argues
stories.summary: An editorial in Frontiers in Nutrition argues that nutrition research should stop treating diet, sleep, activity and wellbeing as separate variables, since eating habits rarely change in isolation, Bioengineer reports.

stories.title: Adenoid surgery alone had fewer complications in children's sleep surgery
stories.summary: A retrospective study from Tampere University Hospital in Finland found children with sleep disordered breathing who had only their adenoids removed had far fewer complications than those who also had tonsils removed, though they needed repeat surgery more often.

stories.title: A brain circuit helps mothers wake to their pups' calls
stories.summary: Researchers studying mice have found a brain circuit that helps mothers wake when their pups call, Medical Xpress reports. For many new mothers, a newborn's crying wakes them even when another caregiver is present and could respond.

stories.title: A hot bath lowered blood pressure more than a bike workout in a small study
stories.summary: In a small study, 30 minutes in a hot bath lowered blood pressure more than 30 minutes of cycling, Verywell Health reports. Experts say baths should not replace exercise but may help people who cannot exercise regularly, and some should check with a doctor first.

stories.title: Chronic back pain may become tied to the brain's sense of self
stories.summary: UC San Diego researchers found movement triggered pain in chronic lower back pain activates a brain network linked to self awareness and memories, which ordinary acute pain usually switches off. It may help explain why painkillers often give limited relief, ScienceDaily reports.

stories.title: Overtraining kept dopamine high in rest periods in mice
stories.summary: Brazilian researchers writing in Neuroscience found mice on an exhaustive exercise routine had dopamine in the hippocampus stay elevated when they should have been resting. If confirmed in people, it could help explain anxiety and insomnia in overtrained athletes.

stories.title: Three weekly band sessions beat two for strength in women around 75
stories.summary: A randomised trial found 12 weeks of low load elastic band training improved fitness in women averaging 75 whether they trained twice or three times a week, but the three session group gained markedly more grip strength and HDL cholesterol.

stories.title: Elastic band training improved balance in older adults with sarcopenia
stories.summary: A 12 week elastic band programme improved functional performance, balance and gait symmetry in 120 older adults with sarcopenia, in a single arm study from Jilin Sport University published in Frontiers in Physiology. With no control group, the gains are hard to attribute.

stories.title: Adding spine mobilisation to physio eased neck pain more in a trial
stories.summary: A randomised trial of 79 adults at a rehabilitation centre in Bangladesh found adding upper and mid thoracic spine mobilisation to standard physiotherapy reduced mechanical neck pain and disability more than physiotherapy alone.

stories.title: Jane Fonda, 88, still exercises every day, just slower
stories.summary: The woman whose 1980s videos had millions jumping in their living rooms now walks and does strength, balance and flexibility work at a gentler pace. 'I essentially do everything I used to do, just slower,' Fonda said, Grazia reports.

stories.title: How long to walk for blood sugar and blood pressure
stories.summary: A 10 minute walk after eating can help lower post meal blood sugar spikes, and walking 20 to 40 minutes three to five times a week may help lower blood pressure, Verywell Health reports. The usual target is 150 minutes of moderate exercise a week.

stories.title: A cold shower habit brought personal benefits, a Basel study finds
stories.summary: University of Basel psychologist Dr Lena Glaser asked study participants to take cold showers, to test whether people adopt climate friendly habits that also offer personal rewards. Those who stuck with the routine reported several benefits, News-Medical reports.

stories.title: Cycling models do not predict interval running well
stories.summary: A study in Physiological Reports found the widely used W prime balance models, borrowed from cycling to track work capacity above critical power, break down when applied to high intensity interval running in trained adult runners, Bioengineer reports.

stories.title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu kept squatting into her ninth month
stories.summary: Actor Samantha Ruth Prabhu posted a video comparing her workouts in the first and ninth months of pregnancy, showing weighted squats in both, Hindustan Times reports. She often posts her progress at the gym.

stories.title: Diet and exercise put type 2 diabetes into remission for over half of younger adults
stories.summary: In a trial reported by the European Association for the Study of Diabetes, 54 per cent of participants under 45 on an intensive low calorie diet and structured exercise programme reached remission in six months, against 4 per cent on usual care.

stories.title: Vegans had lower gut bacterial diversity in a Danish study
stories.summary: University of Copenhagen researchers studying 75 vegans and 75 omnivores expected vegans to have the healthiest gut microbiome. Diversity was lower on average among vegans, News-Medical reports. The researchers called it a major surprise.

stories.title: Peels and stalks may be the fibre most people are missing
stories.summary: UK researchers say fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks are an overlooked source of dietary fibre, and encourage root to tip eating, including watermelon rind and pineapple core, the BBC reports. The bin, it turns out, was the pantry.

stories.title: Animal protein linked to lower testosterone in Finnish men
stories.summary: In 2,546 Finnish men aged 42 to 60, more animal protein was linked to lower total testosterone and more plant protein to higher levels, Nutrition Insight reports. The differences were small, and the cross sectional design cannot establish causation.

stories.title: Regular tea drinking linked to lower vascular disease risk
stories.summary: A study in the Journal of Internal Medicine followed 485,934 adults in China for just over nine years and suggests regular tea drinkers may have a lower risk of vascular disease, the Mirror reports. The study is observational.

stories.title: Plant based grocery packages linked to better health in a small study
stories.summary: Adults who received plant based grocery packages from a Boston area food pantry were in better overall health after a couple of years, researchers report in Preventing Chronic Disease. The study involved 68 adults, and the authors say longer programmes are needed.

stories.title: A survey of 1,203 adults looks at why we reach for comfort food
stories.summary: A cross sectional study in the British Journal of Nutrition examined how UK adults' expected feelings about foods, from chocolate to roast dinners, relate to diet quality and comfort eating, News-Medical reports. It also looked at how branding relates to those expectations.

stories.title: A healthy diet linked to lower heart risk in cancer survivors
stories.summary: A study in JACC: Advances found several healthy eating patterns were associated with better cardiovascular outcomes and longer life expectancy among cancer survivors, for whom heart disease is a leading cause of non cancer death, Medical Dialogues reports.

stories.title: The Planetary Health Diet scored well on nutrition in a Turkish study
stories.summary: Researchers assessing 300 adults at a diet clinic in Turkey found closer adherence to the plant forward Planetary Health Diet was linked to better diet quality and perhaps a smaller environmental footprint, MindBodyGreen reports. It does not require cutting out meat or dairy.

stories.title: Stress and workdays may undo healthy eating plans
stories.summary: A mixed methods study of 232 university employees in Saudi Arabia examined how dietary habits, nutrition knowledge and stress relate, MindBodyGreen reports. The magazine says the findings challenge common assumptions about why people struggle to eat well at work.

stories.title: Researchers document 75 edible beetle species in Northeast India
stories.summary: An ATREE study documented 75 beetle species eaten by Indigenous communities across Northeast India. Of these, 24 are reported as edible for the first time anywhere and five are new records of edible use in India, the New Indian Express reports.

stories.title: Mild cold prompts muscles to release a molecule tied to longevity
stories.summary: A Nature study led by molecular biologist David Vilchez at the University of Cologne found mildly cold temperatures trigger muscle tissue to make, store and release a metabolite called BH2, which helps maintain protein balance in other parts of the body, ScienceAlert reports.

stories.title: Layne Norton's longevity basics, and what he skips
stories.summary: Health.com reports on the habits Layne Norton prioritises for longevity, arguing trendy practices can distract from habits with stronger evidence: movement, nutrition, sleep and time with people you care about. The unglamorous list keeps winning.

stories.title: Stress in both childhood and adulthood linked to more chronic disease
stories.summary: A prospective study of 13,806 middle aged and older adults in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study found those with stressful life events in both childhood and adulthood had a higher risk of several chronic diseases, in Archives of Public Health.

stories.title: Citicoline tested for everyday memory in healthy older adults
stories.summary: A study tested whether daily citicoline could improve memory in healthy older adults with age associated memory impairment, MindBodyGreen reports. The piece notes that some memory changes with age are normal.

stories.title: Scientists question a reported gut bacteria and sarcopenia link
stories.summary: A correspondence in Aging Clinical and Experimental Research raises statistical and biological objections to a cross sectional study that linked 12 gut bacterial genera to sarcopenia in 293 older adults in Iran, Bioengineer reports. Peer review, continuing after publication.

stories.title: Psilocybin showed anti inflammatory effects in a small Parkinson's study
stories.summary: A JAMA Psychiatry analysis drawn from a trial of psilocybin therapy in 12 people with Parkinson's disease and depression or anxiety offers some of the first human evidence of anti inflammatory action, The Microdose reports. It was a safety and feasibility study.

stories.title: Hyperbaric oxygen for post stroke swallowing shows promise, but evidence is weak
stories.summary: A meta-analysis in the European Journal of Medical Research pooled randomised trials of hyperbaric oxygen for swallowing problems after stroke and tested whether the evidence is actually strong enough. Its conclusion is that the evidence is still weak.

stories.title: Washington State gets $7.5 million to study kratom and chronic pain
stories.summary: Washington State University researchers led by Mary Paine received $7.5 million from the NIH to study how kratom works, its risks and its effect on sleep and quality of life in chronic pain, Pain News Network reports. The grant arrives as governments look to ban various forms of kratom.

stories.title: Can gua sha really sculpt a jawline?
stories.summary: Hindustan Times asked dermatologist Dr Akila R of Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru, how much of the online claim that gua sha can sculpt the jawline holds up. The traditional Chinese facial massage can improve circulation and reduce puffiness, the piece says.

stories.title: Uttar Pradesh bars 19 more Ayurvedic practitioners over forged degrees
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Ayurvedic, Unani and Tibbi Medical Systems Board has cancelled the registrations of 19 more Ayurvedic practitioners whose degrees were found forged on physical verification, barring them from treating patients, The 420 reports.

stories.title: Acupuncture clinic opens in Raymond Terrace with registered practitioners
stories.summary: Maitland Wellness Centre has opened a clinic in Raymond Terrace with two acupuncturists registered with Australia's health practitioner regulator, both holding university degrees, News Of The Area reports. Treatments are covered by most private health funds.

stories.title: Adjunct therapies linked to stopping opioids in German primary care
stories.summary: An analysis of insurance claims for 94,125 patients prescribed opioids by German general practitioners in 2021 found 45.5 per cent had no opioid prescription by year end, and adjunct therapies were tied to higher odds of stopping, Bioengineer reports.

stories.title: Chiropractors in a trial felt torn between patients and protocol
stories.summary: A qualitative study in Chiropractic and Manual Therapies describes how 15 chiropractors acting as co-researchers in a Norwegian neck manipulation trial felt pulled between their patients, the research protocol and their own livelihoods.

stories.title: CBD injections changed the gut microbiome in mice
stories.summary: Mice given daily injections of pure CBD for four weeks showed changes in their gut bacterial community, a study in Current Genetics reports. CBD has reached health food shelves fast, and scientists still know little about what it does in the body.

stories.title: DW looks at combining natural therapies with conventional medicine
stories.summary: DW's In Good Shape follows Stefanie Bibo, who lives with multiple sclerosis, as she tries gentler methods such as yoga, fasting mimicking and meditation alongside conventional care, and asks whether they ease her symptoms. It also explains Kneipp therapy.
